table_title: Which US states have generally warm or mild climates, with their state capital's Köppen climate class and annual mean temperature?
db_analog: SELECT state, capital_koppen_class, state_capital, capital_annual_mean_temp_f FROM us_states WHERE capital_koppen_class IN ('Cfa','Csa','Csb','BSh','BWh','As','Aw','Af','Am') ORDER BY state
temporal_note: Wikipedia Köppen climate classification anchor + List of capitals in the United States (universe anchor establishing the full 50-capital domain) + 23 per-capital-city Wikipedia articles for included states + 10 per-capital articles for excluded states with cited evidence (Carson City NV, Santa Fe NM, Columbus OH, Jefferson City MO, Salt Lake City UT, Topeka KS, Indianapolis IN, Hartford CT, Providence RI, Springfield IL), accessed 2026-04-28. Köppen classifications are stable historical-baseline measures (1991-2020 normals are the current standard). Capital annual mean temperatures are 1991-2020 normals from Wikipedia per-capital climate data tables. Where a capital's Wikipedia article includes multiple climate tables (e.g., Frankfort KY has both Downtown and Capital City Airport tables), the canonical 1991-2020 Capital City Airport value is used for consistency with other capitals. The inclusion criterion is anchored to the state CAPITAL's Köppen class — states qualify if their capital's Köppen class is in the warm or temperate Köppen subset {Cfa, Csa, Csb, BSh, BWh, A* (As/Aw/Af/Am)}. For boundary cases where a capital's article notes both Cfa and Dfa classifications under different isotherm conventions (Topeka KS, Indianapolis IN, Hartford CT, Providence RI, Springfield IL — all described as Dfa primary bordering on Cfa), this instance commits to the standard Köppen-Geiger 0°C (32°F) isotherm; capitals whose January mean is below 0°C (32°F) are Dfa under the standard convention and their states are excluded.
_extraction_notes: Multi-source qualitative instance: 2 anchor articles (Köppen climate classification + List of capitals in the United States) + 23 per-capital-city articles for included states + 10 per-capital-city articles for excluded states with cited evidence = 35 source URLs. The List of capitals article anchors the full 50-capital universe so the inclusion/exclusion universe is source-supported even for capitals not individually cited. Inclusion criterion is the state CAPITAL's Köppen class being in the warm or temperate subset {Cfa, Csa, Csb, BSh, BWh, A*}. 23 states qualify: Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, New Jersey, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia. Excluded with cited per-capital evidence (10): Nevada (Carson City BSk), New Mexico (Santa Fe BSk), Ohio (Columbus Dfa), Missouri (Jefferson City Dfa), Utah (Salt Lake City Dsa), Kansas (Topeka), Indiana (Indianapolis), Connecticut (Hartford), Rhode Island (Providence), Illinois (Springfield) — the latter five all described in their per-capital Wikipedia articles as Dfa primary bordering on Cfa under the standard 0°C Köppen-Geiger isotherm convention this instance commits to. Other US states are excluded by the same per-capital criterion (capitals in Dfa/Dfb continental, BSk cold semi-arid, etc.) but their capital articles are not cited individually because they are clearly outside the warm subset; the List of capitals universe anchor confirms they are part of the 50-capital domain. Capital Annual Mean Temperature is 1991-2020 climate normal from each per-capital Wikipedia climate data table; for capitals with multiple tables (Frankfort KY: Downtown vs Capital City Airport), the canonical 1991-2020 Capital City Airport value is used (56.5°F for Frankfort). Across 3 audit cycles: cycle-1 found 3 BLOCKING + 2 hygiene; cycle-2 found 2 BLOCKING (universe-anchor + Frankfort temp); cycle-3 found 1 BLOCKING (other Cfa/Dfa boundary capitals not cited) + 1 hygiene (stale narrative numbers). All addressed. PK on State. Result: 23 rows × 4 columns, 0 duplicate primary keys.
